engagement_title: Pulsevault warehouse night recap: build a same night post set out of eleven phone clips, recover the painted wall mark that has to survive on a dark cover, and hand back the event wording as a working file
vertical: Party, events and promotion, independent monthly warehouse club night, social first promotion with a door paid audience (Cleveland, Ohio)
real_brief_anchor: Verbatim anchor from the Freelancer.com brief quoted in the ledger's grounding_note: "I'm seeking a talented video editor to create high-energy, 30-second recaps of club nights. These videos will be used to promote future events and need to capture the vibrant atmosphere of our nights." Its stated requirements are "30-second videos", "Recaps of club nights" and an "Energetic and fast-paced vibe", with ideal skills calling out "engaging, dynamic content" for event highlight reels. The promoter and venue are laundered to the coined, IP clean night Pulsevault; no real venue, brand, artist or trademark is named. REASONABLY ENRICHED to sit inside the honest capability boundary and to be the fuller commission the same promoter actually needs: the literal post is a frame accurate Premiere and After Effects timeline edit with beat matched cuts and motion graphics, which this connector does not perform, so the recap here is produced by automatic shortening and same source reframing rather than by timeline assembly. Around it sits the rest of what a promoter posts the same night and never commissions separately: a cover still that survives being posted small, the venue's painted wall mark recovered as artwork the night can reuse, and the event details handed back as a working file, because the next date changes every month and the promoter is not going to pay a freelancer for a date change.
client_one_liner: Everything we have from Saturday is phone clips from three of us, the wall mark only exists painted on the brick, and I want it all up before Tuesday when tickets for the next one go live.
client_brief:
Pulsevault, monthly warehouse night, Saturday recap

We run a monthly night in a warehouse space in Cleveland. Door is twenty to thirty dollars, the room is late teens to twenties, and the whole thing lives or dies on what goes up in the days after. Tickets for the next one go live Tuesday.

What we have from Saturday. Eleven clips shot on three of our phones, all vertical, handed over as they came off the devices. Nobody was directing it, so the lengths are all over the place. There is one clip where our host announces the next date over the mic and that has to be understandable, because that is the only place the date exists on camera.

Our photographer sent a handful of stills from the floor, shot fast and dark, and one from a previous night that got mixed in.

The mark. Pulsevault has never had a logo file. It is painted on the brick by the entrance and that is it. There is a photograph of the wall taken at the end of the night under the floodlight. We need it as artwork we can actually put on things, and it has to still be our mark, including on the cover, which is basically black.

What we need. A thirty second recap at full phone size for the feeds. A cover picture for the ticket page and the post, treated so it looks like our room rather than a stock nightclub. The event details for the next date in a working file we can edit ourselves, because next month the date and the lineup change and we are not paying somebody to move a date.

And the cards. We print a little run of lineup cards every month, one per act, and drop them at the two record shops and the coffee place that still put our stuff up. Same card each month off the artwork our print guy holds, we just swap the names, the set times and the picture behind each one. Here is the lineup as a sheet and last month's card. Keep the card the way it is, the running order is the running order do not move it, and put one of Saturday's frames behind each act, not some stock thing.

Make it loud. Our crowd can smell something made by an agency from across the room. It should look like the room felt, not like a beer advert.

Also tell us what to do differently next time so filming is less of a mess.
price_band_and_audience: A twenty to thirty dollar door at an independent monthly warehouse night, with a late teens to twenties crowd who follow the night rather than the venue. The band is load bearing. Push it up into restrained typography, a clean neutral grade, generous white space and a considered logo lockup and it reads as a hundred dollar festival brand or a corporate venue takeover, which is precisely the thing this audience treats as evidence that the night has been bought and is no longer theirs. Push it further down into cluttered stacked promoter text, clip art and drop shadows and it reads as a flyer nobody made, which is a different kind of dead. The correct answer is loud, immediate and slightly rough on purpose: a dark ground, saturated stage colour left in rather than corrected out, display type doing real work, and a mark that looks painted rather than drawn. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even where every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars, and the tight turnaround is the real constraint on how much archaeology is affordable.

brand_identity.sector: Independent monthly warehouse club night, promoted social first to a door paying crowd.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, Cleveland, Ohio, an independent monthly warehouse night run by a small promoter crew.
brand_identity.about: Pulsevault is an independent monthly club night in a Cleveland warehouse, run by a small crew and promoted almost entirely on social in the days after each event. Door is 20 to 30 dollars, the room is late teens to twenties, and the night lives or dies on what goes up before the next tickets drop. Its audience follows the night, not the venue, and can smell something made by an agency from across the room.
brand_identity.audience: Late teens to twenties, following the night rather than the venue. They read agency polish as proof the night has been bought and is no longer theirs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A 20 to 30 dollar door at an independent monthly night. Positioned deliberately rough: loud and immediate, kept clear of both a 100 dollar festival brand and a homemade flyer nobody made.
brand_identity.typography: Display: a heavy, loud display cut doing real work, painted or condensed, with attitude. Text: a plain grotesque for the lineup and details, legible at story size. Loud, never corporate, never clip art. The type should feel like the room, not an advert.
brand_identity.voice: Direct and hyped but never fake, written the way the crew actually talks. Example line: 'Saturday. Warehouse. Tickets Tuesday. Do not sleep on it.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Pulsevault has never had a logo file. The mark exists only hand painted on the brick beside the entrance and survives as one photograph taken at the end of the night under a single floodlight. The wordmark has to be recovered from that photograph as artwork the night can reuse, and it has to hold on a cover that is close to black. There is no colour spec and no prior guideline. The one thing the night reprints unchanged is a plain lineup card its print shop runs a small batch of each month, supplied as last month's flat press artwork: the running order and the per act details change every date, the layout does not.
brand_identity.values: It belongs to the crowd: made by the people who run the night, not bought in.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_saturday_clips/ (11 vertical phone clips, three devices)
assets_supplied.kind: Vertical clips shot on three different phones across one night and handed over untrimmed as they came off the devices, wildly varying length.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Eleven clips from three of our phones. Nobody was directing it so the lengths are all over the place."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Eleven files is not eleven moments. Two of them are the same drop captured from two phones a few feet apart, so cutting both puts the same moment in the recap twice, and the longest file in the folder is mostly the inside of a pocket after a phone was put away, with the audio continuing loud and unbroken, which is exactly the material an energy led automatic cut is drawn to. The genuinely usable pool is a good deal shorter than the folder implies, and the cutting tool can only shorten what it is given.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_floor_stills/ (7 stills, fast lens, high ISO)
assets_supplied.kind: Stills the night's photographer shot from the floor, wide open and pushed, plus one frame from a previous night that got mixed in.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "A handful from the floor and one from another night that got mixed in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frame with the best crowd energy is the one where the crowd's shoulders and the dark ground sit at almost the same value, so a knockout bites into the edge there and reports success, and the frames are already noisy from being pushed, so a heavy grain or halftone treatment on top closes faces into mush at the size the cover actually posts while looking strong at full size. The stray frame from the previous night was lit by a different rig and nothing in its filename says so.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the venue's wordmark hand painted on brick beside the entrance, shot at the end of the night under a single warm floodlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The mark only exists painted on the wall. This is the only picture of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is painted lettering on a photographed masonry substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan: a prompt naming the wall returns the brick rather than the paint, the letterforms have enclosed counters that background removal cannot punch and returns as a solid plaque, and the trace arrives with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it. The right third of the wall falls away from the floodlight into shadow where paint and brick run close in value, and the hand painted strokes are thin where the brush lifted.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_next_date.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The details for the next night: date, doors, lineup in running order, age policy, door price and the ticket link.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything for the next one. The lineup order matters."

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_last_flyer.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of last month's flyer the promoter made himself on his phone, supplied as a tone reference rather than as artwork.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the energy. Do not copy it, it was made on my phone at four in the morning."

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The flat press artwork the night's print shop runs for its monthly lineup card: one A6 card, a near black ground with a full bleed floor still behind a painted style masthead, one act's name and slot, a set time and a billing pill.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last month's card. Keep it the way it is, we only swap the names, the times and the picture."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It reads as four tidy fields over a photo, but the act name, the slot and the set time are one continuous text story in a single frame rather than three addressable fields, and the mapping readout for that frame silently omits the billing run while keeping its line break, so every offset computed past it is short by exactly that run and the validator still returns valid. The act name sits in a fixed measure that does not spill, so a value longer than last month's stops rendering at trim with no overset flag. The picture area is a real graphic frame but at a fixed tall card proportion unlike the landscape cover crop, so a frame cut for the cover cannot be reused and each act needs its own crop to the card's proportion. The media box equals the trim with no bleed box, so a press ready with bleed delivery cannot be honoured from it however the render is called.

assets_supplied.name: pulsevault_lineup.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The next date lineup as a sheet, one row per act in running order: slot, act name, set time, billing and the frame to sit behind each card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The lineup as a sheet. The order is the order, do not move it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The set times are typed inconsistently across the rows the way the promoter typed them, one act's picture cell is simply blank because no frame was picked for it and no header reveals it, and the headliner's picture cell points at the one floor still that came from a previous night under a different rig, whose neutral filename says nothing, so a run that trusts the sheet prints another night's cool lit frame behind the most visible card. The running order is load bearing and must not be reordered, and the date itself is not in the sheet because it is fixed template text on the card.

acceptance_bar: The recap runs at the length asked and is genuinely made of different moments: no shot appears twice from two phones, and nothing from after a phone was put away survives into it.

The recap is delivered at full phone size and nothing was enlarged to get there. If the usable pool cannot carry the length asked, the shorter honest cut is delivered and the shortfall is named rather than padded.
The host's announcement of the next date is intelligible in the delivered audio, because it is the only place that date exists on camera.

The cover reads as this room on this night: one ground, one cast, saturated stage colour left in rather than corrected out, and faces still readable at the size it actually posts. A treatment that looks strong at full size and closes faces into noise at posting size fails.
The cut edge on the cover holds where the crowd and the ground run close in value, judged at full resolution rather than at preview scale.
No frame from a different night is delivered as part of this night's set.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and its counters open and its strokes present at the size it actually sits on the cover, over the dark ground, not at canvas size.
Nothing delivered is a flattened picture of a layout. The mark arrives as vector shapes and the event details as text the promoter can retype when the date moves.
Every canvas in the working file keeps its own size and every one of them was looked at, not only the first one.
One type system across every canvas, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
It reads as a twenty to thirty dollar warehouse night: loud, immediate, slightly rough on purpose. Restrained agency polish fails this brief even where every technical gate passes.
The note names what was applied, every resize any tool reported, which clips were unusable and why, and what to change about next month's filming.

The next date lineup card run is one card per act in the sheet's running order, page count equalling act count, each card carrying that act's own name, slot and set time and its own frame from this night, with the running order never reordered and no card carrying a frame from another night.

The card design is kept as the print shop's artwork and only the per act details change, every per act value renders whole at trim, the act with no chosen frame is handled deliberately rather than left as a hole, and anything the supplied press file cannot carry, its lack of bleed included, is reported rather than faked.

adobe_surfaces.tools: media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut (shortens only), video_resize (never enlarges)
adobe_surfaces.role: The recap itself. It reads the eleven clip pool to work out how much genuinely distinct material exists, cleans the host's announcement so the next date is intelligible, cuts toward the length the promoter asked for knowing the tool can only shorten what it is handed, and brings the result to full phone size while reading what came back rather than what was requested.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_apply_halftone, image_add_grain, image_apply_monochromatic_tint, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs and upscale_factor), image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision plus the mark recovery. It triages the stills, grades the hero to a club target that keeps stage colour rather than neutralising it, applies the treatment as a confined move so faces survive it, recovers the painted wordmark at ink level off a photographed brick wall with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you, and cuts one per act picture from the graded this night masters to the lineup card's own proportion, which is the loop the merge forces back to imaging.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as mapper and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles with an at prefixed picture column), document_render_layout (createSeparateFiles, resolution)
adobe_surfaces.role: The next date lineup card run, the one genuine one record per act job here. The print shop's flat card PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, offsets computed from the document's own reconstructed story text rather than the mapping readout, each act's own graded this night frame bound per row through a prefixed picture column, and the run has to reach the promoter's phone as proofs whose order and identity actually match the load bearing running order rather than a returned list that reports success while reversing it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The cover canvas and the event details sheet as one native editable document carrying a root per format the promoter posts to, each keeping its own canvas size. The graded still must be carried as embedded image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, the recovered mark goes in as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper so it stays editable and stays on the canvas, and the details stay live text so next month's date is a retype rather than a re commission.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The display and detail type carrying every canvas. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land loud rather than corporate at a twenty to thirty dollar door. Numeric weights are non standard per family and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavy weight, every name must be laundered into canonical form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one clean, camera scale low light frame the promoter does not have, for the ground the event details sit on where his own pushed frames are too noisy to carry type, IP clean and with generative candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the same night selects the promoter signs off from on his phone, placed within the per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface against a Tuesday deadline.
trajectory.judgement: Four natures: a cut that can only be shortened, raster work with a treatment decision, details the promoter edits monthly which only an authored fixed canvas document gives back, and a fixed design lineup card the print shop runs one per act which only a record per page merge does. The turnaround also decides how much archaeology the mark recovery can afford.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable, the confirmed account tier, and a time budget for the mark.

trajectory.action: Upload every clip, still and the wall photograph through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Eleven clips off three devices with device generated names will not stay straight in anyone's head. A manifest keyed by role rather than by filename is the only thing that survives the run.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by source device.

trajectory.action: Read the whole clip pool: what each clip actually contains, which are the same moment from two devices, which is dead footage, and how much genuinely distinct material exists.
trajectory.judgement: The promoter counted files, not moments. The pool's real size is the constraint on everything downstream, because the cutting tool shortens and never lengthens, so if the material is not there the length asked for is not available at any price.
trajectory.produces: A clip pool reading naming duplicates, dead footage and the usable set, with a realistic view of the achievable length.

trajectory.action: Run the speech pass on the clip carrying the host's announcement, judged on intelligibility over a loud room rather than on a clean waveform.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the next date exists on camera, so intelligibility is a hard requirement rather than a polish step. A pass that flattens the room also flattens the thing that makes it read as a club.
trajectory.produces: An intelligible announcement clip with the setting used recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut the recap toward the length the promoter asked for, then watch the whole result rather than reading the response.
trajectory.judgement: The only levers are the source pool it is handed and the length asked of it; nothing selects which moments it keeps. Watching it through is the only way duplicated moments and dead footage can be accounted for.
trajectory.produces: A recap cut, watched end to end, with what it actually contains written down.

trajectory.action: Bring the recap to full phone size, reading the dimensions that came back against the ones asked for.
trajectory.judgement: The tool will not enlarge, so a shortfall is a fact about the source rather than a parameter to raise, and padding to reach a number is a lie the promoter will see on his own phone.
trajectory.produces: The delivered recap at its real size with the returned dimensions recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview all seven stills and triage them: which belong to this night, where the subject and the ground run close in value, and how much noise each is already carrying.
trajectory.judgement: The promoter's favourite frame and the frame that can survive a treatment are not necessarily the same picture, and one frame is from a different night with a different rig behind it. The triage decides the cover before any adjustment is applied.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering night, cast, noise and subject to ground separation.

trajectory.action: Grade the chosen hero to a club target that keeps the stage colour rather than correcting it away, judging it at the size the cover actually posts.
trajectory.judgement: Correcting a magenta wash out of a warehouse room removes the room. The band asks for saturated stage colour left in, and a technically neutral frame is here a correct looking wrong answer.
trajectory.produces: A graded hero with the parameters applied recorded, judged at posting size.

trajectory.action: Apply the treatment as a confined move rather than a whole frame one, so the texture lands on the room and the faces stay readable.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity is the craft: the treatment belongs on the field around the people, not on the people. The frames are already pushed, so anything applied globally is stacking texture on texture.
trajectory.produces: A treated cover master with the mask polarity and treatment parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the wall mark: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the paint and not the brick, which polarity to trace, and what to do about the third of the wall that falls into shadow. Background removal is the wrong instrument on letterforms with enclosed counters.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark with the ground path stripped and a real viewBox present.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a clean low light frame to carry the event details, filter to photography, exclude generative candidates, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the same room as the graded hero, not the prettiest thumbnail, and keep it doing a supporting job rather than becoming the poster. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a door price and a crowd that reads agency polish as a warning sign. A display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by asking for a heavy weight, and the lineup order has to stay legible at story size.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the print shop's lineup card PDF into a working document and export its interchange form, then read what the conversion actually exposes: how many text frames, how many picture frames, and what each one holds.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed card looks like says nothing about how the file was set. The four tidy fields over a photo may be one flowing story plus one picture frame, and the bleed question is answered honestly here rather than assumed.
trajectory.produces: A working template plus a frame inventory and a mapping strategy chosen from it, with the bleed reality of the supplied file recorded.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the card's true story text from the interchange file, compute every offset from that string rather than from the mapping readout, generate and validate the mapping, prepare the template, then re export and confirm every expected placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout drops the billing run while keeping its line break, so offsets computed from it are short and the validator still returns valid; preparation reports success either way. The only evidence a field landed is finding it in the re exported document.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders are confirmed by inspection, not by a success message.

trajectory.action: Cut one picture per act from the graded this night masters to the card frame's own tall proportion, reconciling the sheet's picture column against the triage: the headliner's cell points at the previous night stray and one act's cell is blank.
trajectory.judgement: A frame cut for the landscape cover does not fit the card's portrait proportion, so each act needs its own crop rather than a reused tile. The sheet cannot be trusted over the triage, so the stray frame is replaced with a this night frame and the blank cell is a decision made before the run rather than a hole found on the printed card.
trajectory.produces: One per act picture at the card's proportion from this night's footage, with the stray reference overridden and the empty cell's treatment stated.

trajectory.action: Run the four rows against the template in running order binding each act's own picture, produce the press file as one card per act and a proof per act for the promoter, then read every delivered card against its own row rather than trusting the returned list.
trajectory.judgement: The running order is load bearing, so the delivery route has to preserve it: a multi record raster proof reports success while handing the cards back reversed, and a file's position in a returned list is not evidence of which act is inside it. One picture repeated across every card is what a naive run ships.
trajectory.produces: The lineup card run and per act proofs, each verified against its row and confirmed to be in the running order.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the cover canvas and a root per format the details are posted at, inline every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper at the size it will actually sit, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how loud the type can go before it stops being the room and starts being an advert.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the cover and the details set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other canvas.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. A successful export is not evidence that anything survived it.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Take the exported canvases to the sizes they actually post at and judge the mark, the type and the treatment on the real ground rather than at canvas size.
trajectory.judgement: Everything so far was judged on a big screen at full canvas. The only judgement that matters is the one made at the size a phone shows it, on a ground that is almost black.
trajectory.produces: A posting size review naming what holds and what does not.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board, add the graded cover, the licensed frame and the delivered stills within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the note covering picture, sound, the mark, the card run and next month's filming.
trajectory.judgement: A partial success reports as success here, and the vector mark and the print bound card run are not boardable so they belong in the note instead. The promoter signs off on his phone the same night, so the board has to be complete the first time, and the note has to name the card run's bleed shortfall and which delivery route was trustworthy.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover naming the card run, its bleed reality and every limitation.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the automatic cut actually assembled out of eleven files that are not eleven moments. Two clips are the same drop from two phones a few feet apart, and the longest file in the folder is mostly the inside of a pocket with the audio still running loud and unbroken, which is precisely the material an energy led selection is drawn toward. The returned cut is the right length, plausibly paced and reports full success, and it contains the same drop twice and a stretch of near black frames under good audio. Nothing selects which moments are kept, and the pool cannot be lengthened, so what is available at the length asked for is a property of this specific night's footage.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the selection happens inside the tool and there is no read ahead of what it will choose, and no parameter excludes a segment. The brief says the clips came off three phones untrimmed and that the lengths vary, which is the promoter's description of his own mess, but nothing states that two clips are the same moment or that one is dead footage, and cutting the pool as handed over is the reasonable first move. The response is a different route rather than the same call again: withhold the duplicate and the dead file and cut from a reduced pool, or accept a shorter recap than the length asked for and say so, since the tool shortens and can never lengthen.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reduce the pool by hand against the clip reading, re-cut from the reduced set, watch the whole result again rather than sampling it, and if the honest material cannot carry the length asked for, deliver the shorter cut and name the shortfall instead of padding it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A promoter posts a thirty second recap on the night his tickets go live in which the same drop plays twice and several seconds are the inside of somebody's pocket, to an audience whose entire relationship with the night is that it is not fake.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered wall mark is still the mark at the size it actually sits, on the ground it actually sits on. Traced from a floodlit photograph of hand painted brick it looks clean and correct at canvas size, with every letterform present. Placed at its real size on a cover that is close to black, the thin places where the brush lifted drop out and the enclosed counters close up, so the wordmark reads as a solid blob of a slightly different colour. The trace tool takes no options at all and nothing in its output predicts this, because whether a stroke survives depends on the paint, the floodlight falloff on the right third of the wall, the reproduction size and the ground colour, all four at once.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that surfaces it earlier, because the mark, the graded cover and the canvas size only meet at the end, and no tuning parameter exists to prevent it. The brief says the mark has to still be their mark including on a cover that is basically black, which is the promoter's requirement rather than a warning that a trace will close its counters, and delivering a clean looking trace is the reasonable first outcome. The response is a different raster preparation rather than a re trace of the same plate: re-prepare the source so the shadowed third carries, or trace from a differently confined selection, or take the mark to a heavier reproduction size on the cover and re-judge, and only then re-author the canvas around whichever answer holds.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the imaging chain, re-prepare and re-select the paint rather than re-running the same trace, re-inject the viewBox and strip the ground path again on the new output, re-place it at its real size on the real ground, and re-export the document around the version that actually holds.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A night whose only mark has always been a painted wall gets handed a logo file that is unusable on the one surface it was commissioned for, and nobody sees it until it is on a ticket page, because at full size on a white background it looked perfect.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the constructs the club look is naturally built from. A gritty warehouse treatment reaches for a screened light leak, a soft glow behind the headline and outlined display type over the crowd, and the importer discards a blend mode, discards a blur outright and drops a text stroke, with the stroked headline arriving fully transparent so the event details are literally not on the canvas. Every one of those returns success with no warning of any kind, and the document's own rendition shows only the first artboard, so any canvas after the first can be checked no other way than by reading the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the drop happens at import and the import is the last step, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several equally reasonable constructions survives, which no response reports and no checklist enumerates. The brief asks for loud and rough rather than for a specific construction, and the acceptance line about nothing being a flattened picture is the promoter's requirement rather than a warning. The response is to build the effect somewhere else entirely: bake the texture into the raster upstream where it is real pixels, and re-cast the display treatment as fills and solid grounds the importer keeps, then re-compose the canvas around what survives.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the treated master upstream so the grit is in the raster rather than in the layout, re-cast the display type as filled rather than outlined, re-author the HTML, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A working file is handed over in which the next date, the doors time and the lineup are invisible on the canvases nobody looked at, and the promoter posts it at midnight on the night his tickets go live, with every step of the export having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the lineup card run preserves the running order the whole night hangs on. The natural way to hand the promoter a card per act to sign off on his phone is a multi record raster proof, and the tool's own description says one output file per row and hands back a list labelled by row number. The list is wrong: the files come back in an order that does not match the roster, so the headliner's card lands where the opener's should and the load bearing running order is silently inverted, and separately the headliner's card carries the cool previous night frame the sheet's picture cell pointed at. Every gate above passes, the count is right, each file is a valid card, and the only way to find out is to open the files and read the act, the slot and the frame inside them against the row they were named for.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it, because the reversal is in the response itself and the response is the only thing an agent that trusts its tools would use to name and order the files. Nothing states it: the sheet says the order is the order, which is the promoter's requirement rather than a warning that a raster run returns its pages reversed, and producing a card per act as a raster set is the reasonable first move. The response is a different delivery route rather than the same call again: a single press PDF whose page order is trustworthy, or createSeparateFiles, or a recordRange loop producing one card at a time so both order and identity are guaranteed, with the stray framed card sent back to imaging for a this night crop first.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the multi record raster route, re run the card set through a route whose page order and record identity are guaranteed, re cut the headliner's picture from a this night master, rename every proof from what is actually inside it, and re read every card against its row so the running order the night depends on survives to print.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A night whose whole pull is its lineup sends a run of cards to the record shops with the headliner billed as the opener and a frame from a different night behind the biggest name, printed and stacked on the counter the week tickets go live, from a run that reported success and the right page count at every step.

deliverables.name: Pulsevault Saturday recap
deliverables.spec: One vertical recap at full phone size, at the length the pool honestly supports, made of distinct moments with no shot repeated from a second device and nothing from after a phone was pocketed, and with the host's announcement of the next date intelligible. Nothing enlarged to reach a size, nothing padded to reach a length, and any shortfall named with its reason.

deliverables.name: Pulsevault cover still, graded and treated
deliverables.spec: One cover from this night's floor stills, graded to a club target that keeps the stage colour rather than neutralising it, with the treatment applied as a confined move so faces stay readable at the size the cover actually posts, and a cut edge that holds where the crowd and the ground run close in value. No frame from a different night included, no output above its source dimensions, and the grade and treatment parameters logged.

deliverables.name: Recovered Pulsevault wall mark
deliverables.spec: The hand painted wordmark recovered from a photograph of brick as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, counters open and strokes present at the size it actually reproduces on a near black cover rather than at canvas size, delivered with a note on the sizes below which it should not be used.

deliverables.name: Cover canvas and next date sheet, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the cover canvas and a root per format the details are posted at, each keeping its own canvas size, with the mark as real vector shapes, the event details as live text the promoter retypes when the date moves, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the promoter edits the document monthly and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Pulsevault next date lineup card run
deliverables.spec: The print shop's lineup card artwork reverse engineered into a live run: one press file carrying one card per act in the sheet's running order, each binding that act's own name, slot, set time and billing and that act's own graded this night frame cut to the card's proportion rather than one picture repeated, plus a proof per act the promoter signs off on his phone. The card design is kept and only the per act details change, every value renders whole at trim, no card carries a frame from another night, the act with no chosen frame is handled deliberately, and the bleed the supplied file cannot carry is named rather than faked. Per card identity and running order confirmed by reading each card against its row rather than by the page count.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the grade and treatment parameters, every resize any tool reported, which clips were unusable and why, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, the sizes below which the recovered mark should not be used, and specific instructions for next month's filming so the pool is usable. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board the promoter signs off from on his phone, with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: Any shortfall against the length or size the brief asked for is named in the handover note with its reason, and nothing was padded or enlarged to reach a target.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the delivered runtime and dimensions against the brief's targets, then check every shortfall against the note's limitations list.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's file has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered vector file: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered still exceeds its source dimensions and no crop tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the dimensions of each delivered still against its source and diff every captured tradeoffs object against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The export returned one slide per format the promoter posts to, each keeping its own declared canvas size.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and the per slide width and height in the export response.

verifiers_auto.text: No image on any canvas resolved to the importer's placeholder, the mark arrived as vector path shapes rather than one picture, and no text element arrived fully transparent.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the returned per canvas markup for placeholder image data, count path shapes in the mark region, and check every text node's colour value for full transparency.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The selects board exists with the expected item count and an empty failed items list after the final call.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the run and compare the act, slot and set time on each page against the sheet row by row in order, then extract the placed image from each card and compare the four against each other and against the sheet's picture column.

verifiers_auto.text: Every placeholder the mapping claimed to bind is present in the prepared template, no card carries the previous night frame, and the row with the blank picture cell resolved to a stated treatment rather than a missing image.
verifiers_auto.how: Round trip the prepared template to interchange format and search its stories for each expected token, then compare each card's bound picture against the this night set named in the manifest and against the triage's stray frame.

verifiers_human.text: The recap is made of distinct moments: no shot appears twice from two phones and nothing from a pocketed phone survives into it.
verifiers_human.how: Watch the recap end to end against the clip pool reading rather than sampling the opening seconds.

verifiers_human.text: The host's announcement of the next date is intelligible over the room.
verifiers_human.how: Play the delivered audio at phone volume and transcribe the date by ear against the details sheet.

verifiers_human.text: Faces are still readable on the cover at the size it actually posts, and the cut edge holds where the crowd and the ground run close in value.
verifiers_human.how: View the cover at posting size on a phone and then at full resolution, looking for closed faces and a bitten edge.

verifiers_human.text: The mark still reads as the painted wall mark at the size it sits on the cover, over the near black ground, with its counters open.
verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on the delivered canvas and against the dark ground, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: The event details are present and legible on every canvas, not only the first one.
verifiers_human.how: Open the exported document and read every canvas in turn against the details sheet, including the lineup order.

verifiers_human.text: It reads as a twenty to thirty dollar warehouse night rather than as a festival brand or a beer advert.
verifiers_human.how: Judge ground, grade saturation, type loudness and how finished the mark looks against the stated band and crowd.

verifiers_human.text: The note tells the promoter something he did not already know, including what to change about next month's filming.
verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and check that every unusable clip, every resize and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are a cut that can only be shortened, which are raster work, which need an authored fixed canvas document and which is a genuine one record per act press run, given that only one surface here composes free form layout and the deadline is Tuesday.
How much of the eleven clip pool is actually distinct material, and whether the length the promoter asked for is available from what is left.
Whether to deliver a shorter honest recap or to keep the length by keeping material that should not be in it.
Whether the speech pass on the announcement is pushed for intelligibility or held back so the clip still sounds like a room.
Which still is the cover: the promoter's favourite frame, or the frame that can survive the treatment at posting size.
How much stage colour to keep. Correcting the wash out removes the room, and a technically neutral frame is the correct looking wrong answer here.
Treatment polarity: the grit belongs on the field around the people, and the frames are already pushed, so anything global stacks texture on texture.

Selection wording on the wall: naming the wall takes the brick, naming the paint's own appearance takes the mark, and background removal on letterforms with enclosed counters is the wrong instrument entirely.
What to do about the third of the wall that falls into shadow, and whether the mark that results is the deliverable or the starting point.

The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a crowd that reads polish as a warning sign, plus the real numeric weight per family and the display cut reached by its own slug.
Whether the licensed frame stays a supporting ground or quietly becomes the poster, which would make the set read as bought.
How loud the type can go before the canvas stops reading as the room and starts reading as an advert.

The lineup card run is one record per act and the running order is load bearing, so which delivery route preserves both order and per card identity, given a multi record raster proof reports success while returning its pages reversed and a PDF, createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop are the trustworthy routes.

What a lineup card looks like for the act whose picture cell is blank, and what to do about the headliner cell that points at the previous night stray, both decided before the run rather than found on the printed card.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image or video model and it returns a generic nightclub: a crowd that was never in this warehouse, a wordmark that is not the one painted on the brick, and a date nobody announced. IDENTITY: the whole value here is that this is Saturday at this room, and the mark must be RECOVERED off a photograph of a painted wall rather than redrawn, because a redrawn mark is a different night's logo and this crowd would clock it. SPEC: the promoter needs a vertical recap at exact phone size that was never enlarged, made of moments that actually happened and do not repeat, with a specific spoken date intelligible in the audio, plus a press file carrying one card per act in the load bearing running order with each act's own this night frame genuinely bound, none of which a generated asset satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the details sheet is defined by being editable, because the date and the lineup change every month and the promoter explicitly will not pay to move a date. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality that no generation performs: did this cut take the same drop twice, does this mark still have counters at the size it posts, did the headline survive the import at all.
doability_proof: Every link sits inside the verified permitted set, six surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO is confined to the four permitted operations only: media_summarize to read the clip pool, media_enhance_speech for the announcement, video_create_quick_cut which shortens only and is never asked to lengthen, and video_resize which never enlarges and is never asked to. No deliverable depends on frame extraction, trim to timestamp assembly, beat matching, motion graphics, burned in captions or format conversion, which is exactly why the event details are an authored editable document rather than a burn in, and why the recap's length is treated as a property of the pool rather than a target to hit. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, single colour saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, halftone, grain, monochromatic tint, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and upscale factor, remove_background and vectorize are all verified headless across live calls. The mark checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry is live, remove_background returns a solid plaque on enclosed interiors, the trace emits no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero, and the tool takes no options at all so every lever is in the raster preparation. Masked effects with deliberate polarity are verified, which is what makes the confined treatment real work rather than a switch. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as both mapper and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles through an at prefixed picture column, and document_render_layout with createSeparateFiles are verified fully headless and synchronous from a bare press PDF, with one card per record for PDF output and page count equal to row count. The lineup card checkpoint rests on documented findings: multi record PNG and JPEG output comes back reversed while the response labels it by row, so a load bearing running order is silently inverted, with PDF, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop as the three verified trustworthy routes; the mapping readout is lossy and shifts every offset past an omitted run while the validator still reports valid; and per row picture binding through additionalImageFiles is confirmed, which is why each act's own graded frame is bound rather than one picture repeated. PDF derived frame granularity is not under the agent's control and no bleed can be introduced into a file whose media box equals its trim, so the bleed shortfall is reported rather than fabricated. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline vector becomes native editable shapes, the product is a genuine editable document findable by asset_search, photographs must be embedded as image data because references render as empty grey boxes at full success, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and the rendition preview is documented as first canvas only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. The importer checkpoint rests on verified drops: blend mode, blur and text stroke are all discarded silently, and stroked text arrives fully transparent. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because an inlined photograph passes the inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with the case sensitivity, the non standard numeric weights and the display cut slug traps all live. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, licensing returns genuine camera scale photography, and boards persist with a hard cap of twelve placements per call where a partial success reports as success. AVOIDED: no text to image, no generative fill or expand, no object removal, no compositing, no upscaling, no OCR, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above twenty files.
